summary: 武帝侄，永定三年即位，破王琳、安集江南，劝农省役，史称天嘉称治；天康元年崩，子伯宗继。
summary_en: Nephew of Emperor Wu, he took the throne in the 3rd year of Yongding, broke Wang Lin, and settled the south, urging farming and lightening corvée — the "Tianjia recovery" of the histories. He died in the 1st year of Tiankang; his son Bozong succeeded.

bio_md:
# 陈文帝 · 主要事迹

陈蒨字子华，始兴昭烈王陈道谭长子，武帝陈霸先之侄。武帝无子，永定三年崩，蒨入继大统，即皇帝位，改元天嘉。文帝有武略：天嘉元年，王琳引北齐之兵南下，文帝遣侯瑱等破之，王琳败走，陈疆稍定；又平留异、陈宝应等割据势力，江南复归一统。

文帝在位七年，劝农省役、整顿户籍，「江左经侯景之乱，民户凋残，帝以宽简治之」，史称「天嘉称治」——陈朝之小康，惟文帝之世。其治虽不及宋之元嘉、齐之永明，然在陈祚三十三年中，已为最善者。

天康元年，文帝崩，年四十五，子伯宗即位，是为废帝。史评文帝：「有武略，能保江表。」陈朝地狭力弱，介于北齐、北周之间，文帝以宽简之政、武略之才，为陈朝赢得十余年安定——惜其早逝，嗣子幼弱，宣帝废侄自立，陈之基业，自此转衰。

> 参考：点校本《陈书》卷003《世祖纪》。

bio_parts_en.value:
Chen Qian, styled Zihua, was the eldest son of Xiao Daotan, Prince Zhaolie of Shixing, and nephew of the founder Chen Baxian. Baxian had no son; on his death in the 3rd year of Yongding, Qian succeeded, changing the era to Tianjia. Wen had real military ability: in the 1st year of Tianjia, Wang Lin came south with the Qi armies, and the emperor's general Hou Zhen broke him, Wang Lin fleeing — Chen's borders were roughly fixed; he then put down the separatist lords Liu Yi and Chen Baoying, and the south of the river was one again.

Seven years he reigned, urging farming and lightening corvée, repairing the registers — "after the Hou Jing storm the households of the river were ruined, and the emperor governed them with leniency and simplicity," the histories calling the Tianjia years well governed. It was not the Yuanjia or the Yongming recovery, but in Chen's thirty-three years it was the best.

He died in the 1st year of Tiankang at forty-five; his son Bozong, the Deposed Emperor, succeeded. The histories say: "of real military ability, he held the south of the river." Cramped between Northern Qi and Northern Zhou, Chen won a decade of peace through his lenient government and his martial gifts — pity he died early, leaving a child heir; his brother Xuan deposed the child, and the foundations of Chen turned toward decline.

> References: the punctuated critical edition of the *Chenshu*, ch. 3 ("Benji of Emperor Wen").
